### Rubylak

Largest of all Linowan settlements, the holy city of Rubylak stands upon a massive, fortified island amid the Silver River. Surrounded by a well-maintained palisade, its every building is ornately carved from redwood harvested in neighboring Halta by Linowan war parties and floated downriver, down to the last plank. No one goes barefaced here. Any who haven’t earned a mask are required instead to don a hood of undyed cloth. Below the neck, Rubylak’s residents favor robes and sashes of dyed woolen cloth, studded leather belts, and knee-high leather shoes with carefully stitched designs and metal inlay. Home to shamans, elders, spirits, and their servants, Rubylak is a place of pilgrimage. Linowan come from villages throughout the region to seek guidance from the wise, negotiate with rivals and enemies on neutral ground, and participate in seasonal ceremonies and rituals. When a noble dies, their body is brought here for funeral rites, followed by a royal banquet celebrating their life and accomplishments.

### The War with Halta

No one knows when the rancor between the Linowan and Halta — a neighboring arboreal nation dwelling in the redwood forests upriver — originally erupted into war. The Haltans blame the Linowan for hunting their

EX3

large game and cutting down rare redwood trees. The Linowan accuse Halta of raiding Linowan settlements and of profaning sacred oak groves with redwood seedlings. Whatever the cause, hostilities have smoldered for centuries, often flaring up into brutal raids. At the heart of the Haltans’ redwoods, their great city Chanta lies nested within the branches of the Oracle Tree, which the Linowan regard with a mixture of awe, fear, and no little envy. They’d try to take Chanta and the Tree for themselves if not for the pact their ancestral enemy made with the Fair Folk, an agreement confining the Linowan to daring redwood-harvesting forays or hit-and-run attacks.

The Linowan practice of outfitting birchbark canoes and traveling upriver into the redwood forest continues to this day. This isn’t solely to provoke the Haltans, although embittered Linowan who’ve lost friends and loved ones consider vengeance a fringe benefit. Redwood is precious to the Linowan, withstanding time and the elements far better than any timber native to the Linowans’ golden-meadowed river valleys. It’s vital to palisades, crannog walls, and pier moorings, and Rubylak’s court offers rich gifts in exchange for it. Thus, logging continues despite the risks.

### Foreign Relations

Travelers’ tales and ancient enmity towards Halta notwithstanding, the Linowan don’t always attack neighbors and passing travelers. Most settlements are friendly and open to foreigners, as they value dependable trade relationships as much as raiding. The Linowan take pains to remain on good terms with foreign merchants to trade handcrafts for desirable goods like precious stones or ingots superior to local bog iron. On the other hand, the Linowan hold warfare in high regard and seek opportunities for plunder. Unfamiliar merchants who don’t offer appropriate gifts are common targets, as are any who show disrespect. And woe be to those who’ve previously cheated the local tribe — or worse, have been known to take slaves anywhere in Linowan lands. Beyond that, bad hunting seasons, vendettas, and envy over severe wealth imbalances all prompt raids on neighboring non-Linowan peoples. The Realm has established loose, cordial ties with the Linowan over the past century through trade overtures, gifts, and occasional shows of force. Outside of Realm ambassadors and Wyld Hunts, contact is largely limited to Immaculate missionaries, and few Linowan show interest in forsaking ancestral gods to venerate the

Dragons. Realm merchants have begun making inroads, however. And the occasional Dynast-led expedition studies local affairs, accompanies redwood harvesting raids in exchange for a share, or organizes a Wyld Hunt. The current high queen knows that the Empress’s disappearance leaves the Great Houses free to do as they will. She’s responded by courting a handful of politically important Dynasts from afar, such as the merchant-triumvir Cynis Falen or the troop-strapped house matriarch Ragara Banoba, hoping to bargain for their support. She hopes that, should her maneuvering prove successful, her Realm allies’ borrowed might will aid her in crushing Halta and its green-haired, tree-loving troublemakers once and for all. Besides Halta, the Linowans’ greatest enemies are the Fair Folk. It’s widely known that the fae haunting the redwood forests prey upon any they catch unawares, and that the Haltans strand Linowan prisoners in the deep forest as unarmed sacrifices for the fae. The Linowan seek to slay or expel any Fair Folk found on their lands, and those suspected of harboring or aiding the fae may themselves face exile among the redwoods.

Prominent Figures

Arkasi, the Linowan high queen, presides over her court in Rubylak, resplendent in her robes of office and exquisitely carved golden sun mask. Coming from humble origins as a minor village chief’s distant cousin, she’s proven her worth and then some every step of her way, primarily through acts of bravery and displays of martial prowess, supported by diplomatic ingenuity. An air of haughty reserve, cultivated and mastered through a decade of rule, conceals her daring nature and keen intellect.

Simas demonstrated brilliance in many fields from an early age. He might easily have claimed nobility for skill in hunting or weaving, but his singing earned the robin’s mask and five-colored mantle marking him as the current entertainer-royal. Charming, sociable, and proud, he relishes the attention and prestige of royalty. He trains many students, regularly visits other royals and nobles, and speaks often in Arkasi’s court. He craves novelty — news both local and foreign, unfamiliar songs and instruments, and exotic luxuries; he presses Arkasi and his peers toward openness to such things, and embraces gifts from Guild-affiliated and Realm merchants.

Kehonna, a veteran raider and former warrior-royal who’s gone on many a redwood-logging expedition upriver, bears a puissant tiger mask. Her combat

EX3

experience against both Haltans and Wyld creatures is legendary among the Linowan. On more than one occasion — most notably battling the Fair Folk cataphract Sharada Crimson-Snow — she’s fought alongside Haltan warriors against the fae. She respects the tree-dwellers’ martial prowess and holds them no ill will, but neither will she stay her hand on her next raid.

Noteworthy Foreigners

Itokal the Younger, an ambitious Guild factor, made his fortune as a merchant-prince by parlaying inherited wealth into trading metalwork and furs along the Silver River. He’s established a presence in the town of Silvertree to invest directly in the Linowan river trade. Hoping that Itokal can grant the Linowan exclusive access to metal goods — forcing Halta to trade with them at significant disadvantage or make do without — Arkasi makes increasingly friendly overtures toward him. Cynis Legat, the Realm’s ambassador to the Linowan, was appointed by the Empress herself. In the years since her disappearance, no Realm messenger has come to recall Legat to the Blessed Isle. Ever practical, she works to secure trade deals for House Cynis before the Foreign Office thinks to recall her. Queen Arkasi, meanwhile, seeks to leverage Legat’s goodwill in exchange for military support.

Sturdy as a redwood, the Immaculate monk Grayling Fights the Current first arrived as part of a Wyld Hunt. Though the Hunt is long over and his associates long since returned to the Blessed Isle, Grayling remained. He’s become good friends with the Linowan chieftain Hadin, who’s converted to the Immaculate faith through the monk’s teachings. This has made Grayling enemies in Hadin’s clan among those who haven’t been forced to convert yet but see it on the horizon. Charismatic in her unshakable confidence, Amerine of the Forest Witches proselytizes a vision of paradise for a select few. Clad in dramatic white and crimson, she seeks out Exalted champions among Silver River peoples, preaching the glory of immersion in the Witches’ Sea of Mind. Covertly, she gathers information on Realm activities in the region and sabotages people’s faith in Immaculate beliefs as part of the Witches’ longterm aims.

### Neighbors

The Ruskan peoples, dwelling downriver from the Linowan, once traded extensively with the Linowan. Their high-quality, elastic wool — frequently

embroidered with intricate pastoral designs — holds dye well and protects against the elements. During Calibration, their clans gathered at the river isle of Fornay for a week-long festival to hear grievances, settle disputes, strike business deals, and swear oaths. But as Threshold commerce penetrated the Silver River, the Ruskan leveraged their location to monopolize trade, reselling goods at high markup to the Linowan and other upriver neighbors. A generation ago, the Linowan warred against the Ruskan, slaughtering them at Fornay and burning their Silver River trading towns.

Today, the Ruskan form two nations, one north and one south of the Silver River. Both remain embroiled in raids and vendettas with Linowan settlements growing amid their old lands, though some still trade with the Linowan, and with Threshold traders who seek them out. A few leaders seek foreign aid to expel the Linowan.

The Gerivan people dwell amid prairies and deciduous woodlands upriver of the Linowan. Oaken palisades surround elaborately carved, painted, and garlanded longhouse settlements. Although they hunt and trap deer and rabbits, they primarily farm grain, vegetables, and fruit, clearing and burning fields after two fallow years and storing surpluses in spacious attics. A thicket of carvings in front of each settlement serves as a shrine to gods, ancestors, and other local spirits. Riverside Gerivan settlements trade with the Linowan and Halta despite both peoples’ mutual hostility, in which they’ve historically refused to take sides. But recent Haltan successes in bribing Gerivan village leaders into alliance have escalated tensions. Offended Linowan increase their raiding of the Gerivan in retaliation, further inflaming the growing divide between the two peoples. Today, the Gerivan reach out to other local peoples, such as the Ruskan or the fur-trading Chociwel, for allies against Linowan aggression.

## Republic of Halta

East of the Silver River lowlands rises a thick forest of fir, oak, ash, maple, and cedar, pocked with verdant bordermarches. Above its canopy loom a scattering of mighty redwoods; its floor is haunted by the Fair Folk. The Haltan people make their homes within these redwoods’ boughs. Their nation, wedged between two Silver River tributaries, comprises a handful of tree-cities linked by a network of aerial bridges and walkways

EX3

### HAUNTED CITIES OF THE SILVER RIVER

Ancient ruins lie scattered throughout Linowan territory and beyond. Trees grow in and around abandoned structures. Broken towers peek above the Silver River’s waters, creating rapids among its currents. Forest stretches unbroken where once roads and farmland spread. The Linowan and their neighbors deem these places cursed and plague-ridden, overrun by hungry ghosts; leaders forbid adventurers from exploring such dangerous places and from bringing anything found there to local settlements.

Recently, foreign scavengers have ignored these warnings, venturing into the ruins to exploit them. Spurred by their successes — and outraged by outsiders profiting from artifacts buried in Linowan lands — bold young Linowan have ventured there unsanctioned as well. Queen Arkasi, at her advisors’ urging, has called for a summit of Linowan leaders and other local peoples to discuss the risks of disturbing the ruins and whatever ancient horrors wait within.

Over a decade ago, the Riverwalk Company, a Guild enterprise based out of Fray, sent soldiers and priests to the ruins of Longwarren — abandoned since the Second Contagion — to clear it of hungry ghosts. They succeeded where prior ventures failed. Merchants and mercenaries have since established a thriving river port and shipyard amid the ruins, although the occasional deathly spirit still rises on occasion. Empress Galina seized the city last year, installing a satrap whose taxes infuriate Riverwalk’s leadership. Buoyed by their success, the Riverwalk Company attempted to do the same farther upriver in Intelm five years later. There, disaster struck. A hooded spirit commanding a flock of plague-ridden, bloodthirsty bat-winged frogs decimated the expedition. Awake and vengeful after long years, the spirit and its amphibian vectors have spread disease throughout the area. Subsequent attempts to cleanse the ruins have failed, creating a stumbling block to Realm and Guild expansion. Intelm’s location along the Silver River requires ships to hug the opposite bank to avoid its inhabitants’ attention.

No sunlight has shone through Celonir’s stained-glass windows for centuries. Today it’s a ghost-filled shadowland through which raiders from the Underworld city of Arkbane ride when the nemissary-champion Ganti Racewinter winds his horn. At Calibration, mortals are welcome to the city, where merchants from both Creation and the Underworld sell their wares in a sprawling market.
